title: Evaluation of the effect of botulinum toxin on refractory upper limb rest tremor in parkinsonian patients, double-blind, placebo-controlled cross-over study
official: Evaluation of the effect of botulinum toxin on refractory upper limb rest tremor in parkinsonian patients, double-blind, placebo-controlled cross-over study : TOX PARK
summary: Main objective: The primary endpoint is the Patient Global Impression-Change (PGI-C) score completed by the patient compared between botulinum toxin injection and placebo injection at  6weeks after the injection on treatment-refractory resting tremor of the upper limb, in patients with Parkinson Disease.

interventions.name: Dysport 500 U, poudre pour solution injectable

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. -	Patients with PD defined according to UKPDSBB criteria;
2. ‐	Hommes et femmes âgés entre 40 et 80 ans
3. -	Patients with troublesome rest tremor assessed by the CGI-S scale ≥ 3 and persistent despite the initiation of ≥ two anti-parkinsonian treatments (levodopa, dopaminergic agonist, anticholinergic), which defines drug-resistant parkinsonian tremor;
4. -	Patients naïve to botulinum toxin treatment
5. -	Patients whose antiparkinsonian treatment has been stable for at least 4 weeks prior to inclusion and for the duration of the study
6. -	Person affiliated with or beneficiary of a social security scheme
7. -	Free, informed, and written consent signed by the participant and the investigator (no later than the day of inclusion and before any examination required by the research).
Exclusion criteria:
1. -	Patients with tremors related to a pathology other than PD
2. -	Patients under legal guardianship, tutorship, or curatorship
3. -	Patients with atrophy of the targeted muscle
4. -	patients with a urinary tract infection at the time of treatment if the patient suffers from urinary incontinence due to neurological detrusor overactivity
5. patients with a history of swallowing or respiratory disorders
6. -	patients with marked clinical or subclinical neuromuscular transmission deficits (e.g., myasthenia gravis);
7. patients with a fixed contracture
8. -	Patients with atypical parkinsonian syndrome
9. -	Patients treated with drugs which have the adverse effect of causing the appearance or aggravation of tremors: lithium, sodium valproate, levetiracetam, benzodiazepines, corticosteroids, thyroid hormones, ciclosporin, alcohol, tricyclic antidepressants, theophillyne, terbutalineantipsychotics (excluding clozapine)  ;
10. -	Patients with hypersensitivity to the active substance or to one of the excipients (human albumin, lactulose);
11. -	Pregnant or breastfeeding women
12. -	Women of childbearing age without effective contraception
